issues.failure_explanation: With the source's definition \hat P(z)=∫ e^{i z'x}P(x)dx, the Fourier inversion identity underlying the proposition is E[P(X)]=(2π)^{-d}∫ Φ(y+iR)\hat P(-(y+iR))dy (up to damping), not the displayed formula. Thus the proposition prices P(-X). The payoff table and experiments instead use the opposite convention \hat P(z)=∫ e^{-i z'x}P(x)dx, for which the displayed formula is correct. The two conventions are incompatible.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the definition of \hat P to ∫ e^{-i z'x}P(x)dx and adjust the damping sign in the payoff assumption (or equivalently use Φ(-·) in the proposition).
issues.overall_effect: The Fourier pricing formula and the definition of g are sign-inconsistent with the payoff transforms and numerical experiments; if read literally, the paper prices the reflected payoff P(-X).
issues.title: Fourier transform sign convention makes the pricing formula price P(-X)
issues.why_classification: A single sign convention correction fixes the formal statement and all downstream formulas without changing the method, rate, or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we expressed the multivariate normal RV with a zero mean and covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$, $\mathbf{X} \sim \mathcal{N}_d(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}})$, as $\mathbf{X} = \boldsymbol{\tilde{L}} \mathbf{Z}$, where $ \boldsymbol{\tilde{L}} \boldsymbol{\tilde{L}}^{\prime} = \boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$ is computed via the Cholesky decomposition of $ \boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$ or $ \boldsymbol{\tilde{L}} = \boldsymbol{P} \boldsymbol{D}^{\frac{1}{2}} $.

issues.failure_explanation: The equality is false: the inverse CDF of a correlated multivariate normal is not obtained by applying the univariate normal quantile componentwise and then multiplying by a Cholesky factor. The mapping u↦\tilde L Φ^{-1}(u) is a valid change of variables, but it is not the multivariate normal ICDF Ψ_{nor}^{-1}(u;\tildeΣ). The subsequent integral formula is correct for this mapping because its Jacobian equals 1/ψ(y), but the claimed relation is mathematically wrong.

failure_location.quote: Based on this representation, we obtained the following relation: $\Psi_{nor}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{u}; \boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}} ) = \boldsymbol{\tilde{L}} \Psi_{nor}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{u}; \boldsymbol{I_d} ) $

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false equality with the correct change-of-variable statement: set y=\tilde L Φ^{-1}(u), note that the Jacobian equals 1/ψ(y), and do not identify this mapping with the multivariate ICDF.
issues.overall_effect: The stated method to evaluate the multivariate normal ICDF via Cholesky and univariate quantiles is invalid. The integral transformation itself remains correct under a different justification, so the numerical algorithm is not invalidated, but the presentation misstates the construction.
issues.title: False relation between multivariate normal ICDF and Cholesky times univariate ICDF
issues.why_classification: The false relation is a local conceptual mislabeling; the integral formula and algorithm remain correct under the proper change-of-variable interpretation.

issues.failure_explanation: The actual ratio r^{NIG} includes the polynomial prefactor from the Bessel asymptotic. Writing A=y'\tildeΣ^{-1}y, the density asymptotic has factor A^{v/2-1/4}=A^{(1-d)/4}, so r^{NIG} has factor A^{(d-1)/4}. In the equality case (ii), where the exponential factors cancel, this factor diverges for d>1. Hence h_1^{NIG} as defined omits a term that controls boundary growth, the limit √det(\tildeΣ) is false for d>1, and the condition δ²T²Δ-2\tildeΣ^{-1}⪰0 is insufficient to guarantee boundedness of r^{NIG}. The recommended equality choice \tildeΣ=2/(δ²T²)Δ^{-1} lies on the boundary and can produce polynomial growth.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the condition to δ²T²Δ-2\tildeΣ^{-1}≻0 (e.g., choose \tildeΣ=(1+ε)2/(δ²T²)Δ^{-1} for ε>0) or include the payoff-transform decay in the boundary analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The NIG dependent domain transformation condition and the proposed equality construction do not guarantee the claimed boundary growth; the theoretical basis for RQMC convergence in the NIG dependent setting is incomplete.
issues.title: NIG dependent boundary-growth condition omits polynomial Bessel factor
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local strengthening of the condition and a slight adjustment of \tildeΣ, preserving the method and rates, but it changes the optimal equality choice and requires re-deriving the NIG dependent guarantee.
